SBV proposes to raise classification criteria for banks

Under a draft circular, which will replace Circular No. 21/2025/TT-NHNN on regulating the rating of credit institutions and foreign bank branches, the SBV proposes various changes regarding the criteria for categorising banks, as well as the assessment of liquidity and capital adequacy.
In the draft circular, the SBV proposes increasing the threshold for the large-sized bank to VNĐ500 trillion starting from the 2027 rating year.

Specifically, the SBV proposes incorporating the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) and the net stable funding ratio (NSFR) into the bank assessment and rating framework, while also adjusting the application of the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR).

The SBV also proposes a roadmap to gradually increase the scoring thresholds for both the average LCR and the NSFR, to be applied consistently across large-scale commercial banks, small-scale commercial banks, and foreign bank branches.
